prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1391; do not mention it.)
text:
I am writing to advise that this office now represents the injured party in connection with the head-on collision that occurred involving your insured. Our client sustained injuries in the incident, and we ask that all further communication regarding this matter be directed exclusively to our office. Please do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person.

We further request that you provide the bodily injury liability limits under the policy issued to your insured, together with a declaration of any other applicable coverage that may be available. Please also confirm the claim number assigned to this matter so that our file can be properly linked to your records.

We ask that your company preserve all evidence relating to the collision. This includes vehicle data and event recorder information, photographs, adjuster notes, recorded statements, repair and total-loss valuations, and any telematics or dashcam footage in your possession. Please suspend any routine deletion or disposal procedures that could affect these materials.

Kindly acknowledge receipt of this letter in writing and confirm your intent to comply with each of these requests within the time allowed by applicable law.
